question: As is known, the former Frontex chief, Fabrice Leggeri, who was forced to resign after OLAF’s damning report, is to run as a candidate in the European elections with France's right-wing RN party led by Marine Le Pen.1 While OLAF’s investigation was still underway, the Greek government presented Leggeri with a medal for ‘his help in managing the migration situation’.

The investigation was completed in February 2022 and included the following findings2: – Frontex’s executive management repeatedly concealed suspicious cases from its own officers and prevented them from investigating; – the agency withdrew aerial surveillance so that violations could not be recorded; – it co-funded some of the Greek organisations that carried out illegal pushbacks and misled the bodies in charge of overseeing Frontex; – the agency continued to take part in joint operations despite the fact that pushbacks very clearly constitute ‘serious or continuous violations of human rights’.
In light of these developments, can the Commission answer the following: 1.
Are EU bodies conducting any ongoing investigation against Leggeri?
Seeing as though it has been established that the Union’s interests have been damaged, has blame been apportioned to any individuals?
Have the details been sent to the European Public Prosecutor's Office or the ordinary courts to establish criminal liability?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (17.6.2024) The Commission can only reply with regard to the European Anti-Fraud Office (OLAF) investigations based on information from OLAF but cannot respond for any other EU body. Whilst OLAF has confirmed that it has both ongoing and closed investigations concerning the European Border and Coast Guard Agency (Frontex), it cannot provide further details.

OLAF cannot confirm or deny the involvement of any specific legal or natural persons in its investigations. This is in order to protect the confidentiality of OLAF’s investigations, of any follow-up action, personal data and procedural rights. OLAF closed an investigation concerning Frontex on 15 February 2022.

Following this investigation, OLAF sent the final report and disciplinary recommendation to the Frontex Management Board – the authority competent for follow-up. The Frontex Management Board made public in April 2022 that the former Executive Director was a person concerned in this investigation1. In its capacity as Member of the Frontex Management Board, the Commission is not aware of any other investigation.
